title: Strict currying for the native reversed ordinary tensor and row-sign Hom
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $Y$ any scheme, and $\mathcal A$ its category of native continuous-coefficient module sheaves, with the ordinary tensor and sheaf-Hom adjunction of [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models]. For arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes $P,Q,I$ in $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $T_o(P,Q)=\operatorname{ordinaryTensorTotal}(P,Q)$. Its degree-$n$ object is $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}Q^q\otimes P^p$, with differential $d_P+(-1)^p d_Q$. Put $B(P,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{row}}(P,I)$, with $B(P,I)^q=\prod_p\mathcal Hom(P^p,I^{p+q})$ and row differential whose projection at $p$ is $(-1)^p(d_I\circ a_p-a_{p+1}\circ d_P)$. Write $\iota_{p,q}:Q^q\otimes P^p\to T_o(P,Q)^{p+q}$ and $\pi_{q,p}:B(P,I)^q\to\mathcal Hom(P^p,I^{p+q})$ for the actual coproduct inclusions and product projections. For every chain map $f:T_o(P,Q)\to I$, there exists a chain map $\phi:Q\to B(P,I)$ such that for all integers $p,q$,
$$\operatorname{uncurry}_{P^p,Q^q,I^{p+q}}(\phi^q;\pi_{q,p})=\iota_{p,q};f^{p+q}.$$
Here underived uncurrying uses precisely the ordinary module-sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction; there is no sign in this equation and $;$ means composition in diagrammatic order. No K-flatness, K-injectivity, derived adjunction or derived representative comparison is assumed.

proof.text: Write $c_{P,Q,J}:\operatorname{Hom}(Q\otimes P,J)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Q,\mathcal Hom(P,J))$ for the ordinary adjunction assumed in the statement. It is natural in all three arguments. Its additivity also follows directly: for fixed $P$, $c(h)=\eta_Q;\mathcal Hom(P,h)$, where $\eta$ is the adjunction unit; postcomposition in sheaf-Hom sends $h+h'$ to the sum of postcompositions, so bilinearity gives $c(h+h')=c(h)+c(h')$ and $c(-h)=-c(h)$. Here the ordinary Hom maps are precomposition and postcomposition, as specified in [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models], and the bilinearity is [def-weil-preadditive-category]. These are identities of module-sheaf morphisms, not assertions about global sections.

proof.text: Set $f_{p,q}=\iota_{p,q};f^{p+q}$ and $b_{p,q}=c_{P^p,Q^q,I^{p+q}}(f_{p,q})$. By the defining universal property of the given product $B(P,I)^q$, the family $(b_{p,q})_{p\in\mathbf Z}$ determines a morphism $\phi^q:Q^q\to B(P,I)^q$ with $\phi^q;\pi_{q,p}=b_{p,q}$. There is no sum in this construction and no finite-support condition on the family. The inverse identity for the same ordinary adjunction already gives $\operatorname{uncurry}(\phi^q;\pi_{q,p})=f_{p,q}$.

proof.text:
Put $A_{p,q}=\mathrm{id}_{Q^q}\otimes d_P^p$ and $D_{p,q}=d_Q^q\otimes\mathrm{id}_{P^p}$. The stated total differential means exactly $\iota_{p,q};d_T^{p+q}=A_{p,q};\iota_{p+1,q}+(-1)^pD_{p,q};\iota_{p,q+1}$. Restrict the chain-map equation $f^{p+q};d_I^{p+q}=d_T^{p+q};f^{p+q+1}$ along $\iota_{p,q}$ and distribute composition. Thus
$$f_{p,q};d_I^{p+q}=A_{p,q};f_{p+1,q}+(-1)^pD_{p,q};f_{p,q+1}.$$
This uses just the definition of a morphism of complexes in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the displayed differential in the item; in particular the sign is indexed by $p$, despite the reversed order of the tensor factors.

proof.text:
Apply $c$ to the last equality. Its three naturality identities respectively give
$$b_{p,q};\mathcal Hom(P^p,d_I^{p+q})=b_{p+1,q};\mathcal Hom(d_P^p,I^{p+q+1})+(-1)^p d_Q^q;b_{p,q+1}.$$
Indeed the first term uses naturality in the output, the second precomposition in the $P$ parameter, and the last precomposition in the $Q$ variable; the additivity verified in step 1 moves the sum and its sign through $c$. Subtract the first term on the right and multiply by $(-1)^p$. Since $((-1)^p)^2=1$ for every integer $p$, this gives
$$(-1)^p\bigl(b_{p,q};\mathcal Hom(P^p,d_I^{p+q})-b_{p+1,q};\mathcal Hom(d_P^p,I^{p+q+1})\bigr)=d_Q^q;b_{p,q+1}.$$
No comparison of derived objects or homotopy classes occurs.

proof.text: By the specified row differential, the left side of step 4 is $(\phi^q;d_B^q);\pi_{q+1,p}$; by the product-lift equations of step 2 the right side is $(d_Q^q;\phi^{q+1});\pi_{q+1,p}$. Equality for every $p$ implies $\phi^q;d_B^q=d_Q^q;\phi^{q+1}$ by the defining uniqueness property of the product. Hence the family $\phi^q$ is a chain map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The uncurry equation in step 2 is exactly the requested equation on the actual inclusions and projections, without a sign. All degrees are arbitrary integers, so this proves the assertion for unbounded complexes as well.
